% note: Bins: each puzzle's Haiku-medium single-sample accuracy at 16 steps over its 5 samples, in 10-point bins with the top bin closed. The bins were fixed, and their occupancy written, before any Haiku-max value was binned; with so few samples some bins cannot hold a puzzle and are empty.
% note: A bin with fewer than 3 puzzles is shown but not read; a shape whose largest bin holds more than 80\% of its puzzles is uninformative, and then only the unbinned curve is read (rule fixed before computing).
% note: Chains (1\ensuremath{\times}16): uninformative: no; the largest bin [0,10) holds 49 of its 80 puzzles (61.25\%); the bins marked read are read.
% note: Pieces (16\ensuremath{\times}1): uninformative: no; the largest bin [0,10) holds 41 of its 80 puzzles (51.25\%); the bins marked read are read.
% note: Haiku-max single sample: the mean over the bin's puzzles of each puzzle's single-sample accuracy. Vote at $k$: Haiku-max's majority vote of $k$ samples as Test~B2 scores it, estimated from the samples drawn; $k$~=~6 (Test~B2's $k$). Vote of all samples drawn: the vote of all 10 Haiku-max samples per puzzle. A missing sample, or a sample with no answer or whose official format is not ok, votes for nothing, and a tie among several leading answers scores an equal share of one right answer when the right answer is among them (the locked vote curve's rule). Means over puzzles, in \%; no intervals.
% note: Puzzles with too few wrong samples: the puzzles in the bin with fewer than two wrong Haiku-max samples, so no agreement between wrong answers can be measured.
% note: Wrong-sample agreement thirds (a post hoc variant of the within-bin split in Study~1's pre-specified vote lookup chart): within a bin, the puzzles with at least two wrong Haiku-max samples are ordered by how often their wrong samples give the same answer (agreeing pairs over pairs; ties broken by puzzle) and cut into a lowest, middle and highest third so that the higher thirds take any extra puzzles. Study~1's chart gives the extra puzzles to the lower thirds and sends a whole group of tied puzzles to the lower third, so these are not its thirds, and a lower third can be empty here (dashes). A bin whose puzzles all have too few wrong samples has no thirds. The rule above on which bins are read applies to bins, not to thirds: each third rests on the few puzzles in its puzzles column.
% note: Haiku-max format compliance: the locked share of the 16-step Haiku-max samples whose official format status is ok, for all puzzles of the shape (pre-specified descriptive); it is not stamped by bin.
% note: The unbinned rows are Study~1b's locked single-sample accuracy and vote curve (pre-specified descriptive); the post hoc recount agrees with them (checked when the table is built). Their vote at $k$ is Test~B2's challenger at that shape: Test~B2 is confirmatory and pools the two shapes, so this per-shape value is a descriptive breakdown, not a test. The binned rows and the thirds are post hoc exploratory, with no causal claim.
